speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with postpartum fever and abdominal tenderness; can you tell me how many days postpartum you are and what your highest recorded temperature has been? Additionally, have you experienced any vaginal discharge or foul-smelling lochia?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old woman. The patient is in the postpartum period after delivering an 11 pound boy vaginally at 40 weeks gestation. She experienced a prolonged course during labor. She reports increased frequency of urination and uterine tenderness. She also mentions a decrease in bowel sounds.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Postpartum Endometritis. (Note: The patient's report of decreased bowel sounds is concerning for an intra-abdominal complication like an abscess or ileus, which often accompanies severe endometritis or surgical injury, but the primary clinical picture of fever, uterine tenderness, and foul-smelling lochia points to endometritis as the initial working diagnosis. I will proceed with this diagnosis pending imaging confirmation.)
